headStaleness: WHY THIS RECEIPT WAS RE-HEADED, and the general trap it fell into. It was first written at a963db1d145c2eebe06d5848919e140d33ada742 and three fields kept saying so while the branch moved four commits past it: currentHead, gateResults[0].head and independentReview.head. The reviewer caught it and was right - it is the rule this session enforced against that same reviewer, turned around, because a gate result recorded at an earlier head does not cover the commits after it. THE STRUCTURAL PART, which outlives this instance: a receipt that records the head it was gated at is, by construction, committed one commit LATER than the head it names, since the commit carrying it is not in it. That one-commit gap is unavoidable and is NOT drift - the gated tree and the reviewed tree are identical, and the only difference is this file. Any gap LARGER than that carrying commit is real staleness and must be repaired before the transition executes. Read the two apart before treating a mismatch as either.
